title: GET /api/orders runs one order_items query per order inside a for-await loop

verification.reasoning: The N+1 is real. api/orders.js:8 loads up to 50 orders, and api/orders.js:9-11 awaits one order_items query per order in sequence, so one request makes up to 51 serial round trips. It is reachable by any authenticated user (src/server.js:14). Two parts of the claim are overstated. First, src/db.js:7-9 calls pool.query, which checks out a connection and releases it after each query. A request therefore holds at most one connection at a time and does not hold several across its round trips, so the pool-exhaustion claim does not hold up. Second, prisma/schema.sql:23 indexes order_items(order_id), so each lookup is cheap, and the fan-out is capped at 50 by the LIMIT at api/orders.js:8. The cost is bounded serial latency, so medium rather than high.

rationale: The handler loads up to 50 orders, then awaits a separate `order_items` query for each one in sequence. A single request therefore makes up to 51 serial round trips, and the default pg pool has only 10 connections.
impact: Latency on the orders list grows with page size, and each request holds pool connections for many round trips. Concurrent users can exhaust the pool.

recommendation.action: Fetch all items in one query with `order_id = ANY($1)`, then group them by order_id in memory. Alternatively, use a single join or json_agg query.

title: Admin export blocks the event loop with execSync and buffers the whole table in memory

verification.reasoning: api/admin.js:13 calls the synchronous execSync to run psql \copy on a whole table inside the request handler. The event loop is blocked until psql exits, which stalls every other request, including /health at src/server.js:12. The whole stdout is buffered and turned into a string before res.send at api/admin.js:14. execSync has a default maxBuffer of 1 MiB, so larger tables make it throw. The route sits behind requireAuth and requireAdmin (src/server.js:15, src/auth.js:16-18), and the reporter already took that into account in rating it medium. I found nothing that streams the output or runs the export asynchronously. The medium severity is correct.

rationale: The handler calls `execSync` to run psql `\copy` on a whole table. The event loop is blocked until the dump finishes, and the full output is then buffered as a string before being sent. execSync's default maxBuffer will also throw on large tables.

evidence.codeSnippet:
const output = execSync(`psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "\\copy ${req.body.table} to stdout csv"`).toString();
  res.type('text/csv').send(output);

impact: While one export runs, every other request on the process stalls, including /health. Large tables fail at the maxBuffer limit or consume large amounts of memory. The route is admin-only, which limits who can trigger it. The command-injection risk on `req.body.table` belongs to the security lens.

recommendation.action: Use async `spawn` and pipe the child's stdout to `res`, or stream with pg-copy-streams. Do not buffer the output.
